Wet-capping only lowers moisture. Division-by-zero guards (dry_available/wet_available>0, total_bu feasibility check before _weighted) all hold. Demo blend computes to ~15.50% moisture (at cap) and ~55.75 lbs/bu (above 55.0 min), so it passes and prints sincere output. No fault found; clean claim holds.

blind_review.description: In _padding_window, padded_start is shifted back by EDGE_MARGIN but padded_hours only adds EDGE_MARGIN once. That single extra hour just compensates for the leading shift, so the series ends at window_end-1. The last hour of the requested window has no right-hand neighbor and can never be detected as an extremum by find_extrema; padded_hours needs to be num_days*24 + 2*EDGE_MARGIN.

metadata_audit.notes: The single fault is in _padding_window: padded_hours = num_days*24 + EDGE_MARGIN adds only one extra hour total, but with padded_start shifted back by one, the series spans start_hour-1 .. start_hour+num_days*24-1. find_extrema (range 1..len-2) never evaluates the last sample, so the final window hour (start_hour+num_days*24-1) has no successor and cannot be flagged as an extremum -- one hour short; should be num_days*24 + 2*EDGE_MARGIN. Keys all fit and none appear verbatim. Files=3, hops report->build_hourly_series->_padding_window=2, distractors (padded_start, EDGE_MARGIN, find_extrema range, window_end filter) plausibly ~4. No other errors; unmarked and no execution display.

blind_review.description: business_days_worked_by loops with `current < cutoff_date`, which excludes the cutoff date itself. But the docstring says it should count business days 'through the accrual cutoff date' (every day worked as of the close), so a business day falling on the cutoff (e.g. Fri July 31) is wrongly dropped from the numerator, under-accruing wages by one day.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is in business_days_worked_by: the loop uses `while current < cutoff_date`, excluding the cutoff date, while its docstring says to count days 'through the accrual cutoff date' (inclusive). July 31 2026 is a Friday/business day, so it is wrongly dropped — a genuine off-by-one that stops one day early, contrasting the inclusive `<=` used in business_days_in_period. 4 files; 3 hops (generate_accrual_report -> compute_accrual_for_employee -> _proration_fraction -> business_days_worked_by); ~5 plausible distractors (build_biweekly_period +13, business_days_in_period `<=`, pto_months_accrued inclusive range, gross_pay_per_period 26, _is_business_day `<5`). Keys are plausible and none appear verbatim. No hint markers; no failing test or fault-displaying output.

blind_review.description: In cone_for_heatwork the search loop runs `for i in range(len(CONE_TABLE) - 1)`, so it never considers the last (hottest) cone as the reached cone. A firing that meets or exceeds the final threshold (275 units, cone '10') gets reported as only cone '6', and the 'units carried past the table's ceiling' branch is unreachable. The loop should range over the full table.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault confirmed in cone_chart.cone_for_heatwork: the loop `for i in range(len(CONE_TABLE) - 1)` never examines the last table entry (cone '10', threshold 275.0), so the highest cone is unreachable and the 'carried past ceiling' margin branch is dead. Classic off-by-one boundary defect. Keys all describe it aptly and none appear verbatim. 5 files; 4 hops (main->run_firing->summarize_firing->evaluate->cone_for_heatwork); ~6 other boundary-ish spots (tick_count/append in controller, _integrate range, active_segment fallback, target_temperature seg_start, next_index/margin) are plausible distractors. No other errors; docstrings/names read sincere; no hardcoded output displays the fault.

blind_review.description: In merge_cluster, the stacked text is built from cluster[:len(cluster)-1], which drops the last cue's text; every source line should be included, so the final overlapping caption is silently lost.

metadata_audit.notes: The one fault is in merge_cluster: `lines = [c.text for c in cluster[:len(cluster) - 1]]` drops the last cue's text, contradicting the docstring that every source line is stacked. Keys (last cue / one element short / off by one / drops the last) all fit and none appear verbatim. 2 files, fault reached across a single import hop into cue_timing; group_overlap_clusters is correct standard interval logic and not a planted distractor. No hint comments, no test/output.

blind_review.description: In _has_capacity, the check returns True (room available) only when available_beds <= num_guests, which is the opposite relation. A booking succeeds only when there are FEWER available beds than requested guests; it should require available_beds >= num_guests.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is in _has_capacity: `available_beds <= num_guests` is backwards; should be `>=`. Matches defect_class 'comparison' and all keys, none of which appear verbatim (code uses `available_beds`, `num_guests`). locality_hops=2 (create_booking -> _check_availability -> _has_capacity), 3 files, ~6 plausible distractors. Single defect, unmarked, no execution output.

blind_review.description: is_recovered checks whether the latest depth is within a margin of the critical (shutoff) level, but recovery means the water table has risen back near its undisturbed baseline, which is static_level_m. It tests the wrong field (critical_level_m instead of static_level_m), so a well sitting right at its dangerous shutoff depth would be reported as recovered.

metadata_audit.notes: The single fault is in is_recovered (models.py): the docstring says 'settled back near its undisturbed level,' i.e. the static level, but the code compares latest_depth_m against critical_level_m + recovery_margin_m instead of static_level_m + recovery_margin_m. static_level_m is defined on Well but never used, confirming the wrong-baseline defect. Keys 'wrong baseline' and 'static level' fit and neither appears verbatim (field is 'static_level_m'). 4 files; 3 hops (generate_compliance_report -> evaluate_well -> recovery_status -> is_recovered). needs_shutoff correctly uses critical_level_m and all other functions are correct, so exactly one defect. No hints or execution output present.

blind_review.description: warp_float_limit returns yarn_set.weft_yarn.max_float_run instead of the warp yarn's tolerance, so warp floats are checked against the weft yarn's limit; both float limit functions read weft_yarn.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault confirmed: warp_float_limit returns yarn_set.weft_yarn.max_float_run (3) instead of warp_yarn.max_float_run (5) — a warp float should be governed by the warp yarn's tolerance. weft_float_limit is correctly the weft yarn. Keys 'warp yarn'/'weft yarn' appear only with underscores or in different phrasings, not verbatim; 'wrong yarn's limit' is absent. 5 files, 4 call hops (main->evaluate_draft->run_structural_checks->check_float_limits->warp_float_limit), and the adjacent correct weft_float_limit is the 1 distractor. Sample reads sincerely with no failing test or displayed output.

blind_review.description: choose_target_lane picks the more heavily loaded lane as the target instead of the lighter one -- for a matched bow/stern pair you want to add the next vehicle to the emptier lane to balance the crossing, but with `bow_lane.current_load_kg > stern_lane.current_load_kg` returning bow, it keeps piling onto whichever lane is already fuller. The comparison direction is inverted (should be `<`).

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is in choose_target_lane: the comparison bow_lane.current_load_kg > stern_lane.current_load_kg returns the already-heavier lane as the primary target, when balancing intent (implied by the fallback design) requires favoring the lighter lane. All claims and constraints hold: two files, ~1 call hop from plan_load to the faulty line, plausible distractors (fits comparisons, sort_queue key), no verbatim key leakage, sincere docstrings, and the __main__ output only prints lane totals without exposing the fault.

blind_review.description: run_irrigation_cycle only catches ProbeConfigError, but should_irrigate raises a plain ValueError for a zone with fewer than MIN_SENSORS_REQUIRED probes; that ValueError is unhandled and aborts the whole cycle, so one misconfigured zone stops every other zone from being checked, contradicting the docstring's promise to check every zone.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault: compute_field_moisture_average catches ZeroDivisionError alongside transient errors, so a zero-length/misconfigured probe (probe_length_cm=0 -> ZeroDivisionError in parse_reading's division) is silently dropped and masked as normal RF flakiness instead of surfacing as a config error. Keys all fit and none appear verbatim (text says 'simply excluded', not 'silently'; no 'zero-length'/'misconfigured'/'too broadly'). Distractors (raw_count range check, Topp coefficients, retry/backoff, vwc clamping, KeyError on probe_configs lookup, MIN_SENSORS check) support ~5. locality_hops is roughly 2-3 depending on whether the trivial evaluate_field wrapper counts; within tolerance. Single genuine exception-handling defect, sincere docstrings, no failing test/output.

blind_review.description: In ledger.py, _reserve_funds catches every non-InsufficientFunds exception (e.g. GatewayTimeoutError) and fabricates an unconfirmed Hold, and commit_bid then proceeds to set current_price/leading_bidder and record the bid anyway. So a gateway failure is swallowed and the bid becomes the leading offer without funds ever being secured, contradicting the docstring's 'once secured, record the bid as the new leading offer.'

metadata_audit.notes: The fault: ledger._reserve_funds swallows GatewayTimeoutError and returns an unconfirmed Hold (confirmed=False), and commit_bid never checks hold.confirmed before updating auction.current_price/leading_bidder_id and recording the bid as the leading offer. A bid whose funding hold never confirmed still wins. Keys 'unconfirmed hold', 'gateway timeout', 'never checks whether' fit and none appear verbatim (code has GatewayTimeoutError/confirmed=False/hold_confirmed but not those exact phrases). 4 files, plausible distractors (rounding, min_next_bid boundary, MAX_JUMP flag, anti-snipe window, seconds_remaining<0 boundary, InsufficientFunds re-raise), locality_hops~3 (submit_bid->commit_bid->_reserve_funds->authorize_hold where the timeout originates). Single defect; no execution output; nothing marks the fault.

blind_review.description: In _attempt_door_close, a bare `except Exception` treats a transient DoorObstructionError (something momentarily in the doorway, a normal recoverable safety event) exactly like a real HardwareFault: it pulls the car OUT_OF_SERVICE and raises DispatchFailedError. The two distinct exception classes are clearly meant to be handled differently, but the overly broad catch collapses them, so an obstruction permanently sidelines an otherwise healthy car.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault confirmed: _attempt_door_close in car.py catches a broad `except Exception`, so a transient DoorObstructionError (which should clear on retry via the decrementing _obstruction_countdown) is handled identically to a real HardwareFault and pulls the car OUT_OF_SERVICE. Keys are plausible descriptions and none appear verbatim (the source uses CamelCase DoorObstructionError/HardwareFault, not the lowercase phrases). locality_hops=4 matches main->dispatcher->scheduler->dispatch_to->_attempt_door_close. The capacity fail-open on SensorNotReadyError is explicitly documented as deferring to the mechanical interlock, so it reads as intentional design rather than a second defect or distractor.

blind_review.description: In evaluate_batch, the broad `except Exception` catches SensorDataError (missing log, no usable readings) and any other unexpected failure and marks the shipment as 'compliant' with 'evaluation skipped, treated as within tolerance'. Shipments that could not actually be evaluated are silently passed as safe, which for a cold-chain compliance check is exactly backwards — they should be flagged or set to an error/unknown status.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is the catch-all `except Exception` in evaluate_batch, which sets status to 'compliant' and swallows errors (e.g. SensorDataError from a missing log or no readings), treating failures as passing. Keys all fit and none appear verbatim (code has `except Exception` but not 'catch-all except'; 'compliant' appears but not the phrase 'marks it as compliant'). files_spanned=2 and locality_hops=1 (main -> evaluate_batch) are correct; distractor_count=1 fits (the single-reading zero-duration case in _excursion_minutes is a plausible pause point). Exactly one defect; excursion math is otherwise correct.

blind_review.description: In consume_fuel, burning fuel removes mass from the truck, so gross weight should decrease by the burned fuel's weight -- but the code adds it (self.gross_weight_kg += burned_weight_kg), inflating the truck's weight as it drives.

metadata_audit.notes: Sign fault confirmed in FleetTruck.consume_fuel: burned fuel leaves the tank so gross_weight_kg should decrease, but the code does '+=' burned_weight_kg. locality_hops=2 (plan_daily_route -> build_route -> consume_fuel), files_spanned=3, compact_load serves as the single plausible distractor (correct '-='). No keys appear verbatim (code uses underscored identifiers). No hints, no output.

blind_review.description: Holds are supposed to push the membership period further out to credit back the paused days, but apply_hold_adjustment subtracts the hold days from the boundary, pulling the expiry earlier instead of later -- so a paused member gets less time, not more.

The raw load-cell reading runs HIGH above the reference temperature (per the docstring, calibration should remove that excess), but corrected_weight ADDS the thermal drift instead of subtracting it, making the correction worse rather than removing it. The humidity correction (which restores a suppressed reading) correctly adds, so the two directions are inconsistent.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault is in calibration.py corrected_weight: the comment states raw load-cell readings run HIGH above the reference temp and calibration must remove the excess, so the positive drift should be subtracted, but the code does raw_weight_kg + drift (wrong sign, amplifies the drift). corrected_humidity is the correct parallel (raw runs low, so adding is right) and serves as a distractor. Keys all plausible and none appear verbatim. Locality path monitor.run_monitoring_cycle->evaluate_alerts->compute_nectar_flow_rate->compute_net_weight_change->corrected_weight = 4 hops. 5 files. Distractors (corrected_humidity, alerts weight_change_48h reconstruction, harvestable tare/reserve subtraction) ~3. Single defect; nothing else wrong.

blind_review.description: In compute_priority_score, prior denied boardings are subtracted from the score, which pushes previously-bumped passengers toward the back of the standby list. Given the name PRIOR_BUMP_WEIGHT and the norm that involuntarily bumped passengers earn compensating priority, this term should be added, not subtracted.

In summarize_run, total_transit_ms is a sum of elapsed milliseconds but it is added directly to trap_purge_time_s (seconds) as if it were seconds; it should be converted with pig_units.ms_to_s first. The resulting downtime is off by a factor of 1000.

In _accumulate_duration, elapsed_seconds is tracked in seconds but CROSSFADE_MS (500, a millisecond value) is subtracted directly from it, so each crossfade removes 500 seconds instead of 0.5 seconds. It should subtract CROSSFADE_MS / 1000.0.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault: in scheduler._accumulate_duration, elapsed_seconds (seconds) has CROSSFADE_MS (500 ms) subtracted directly, so it removes 500 s instead of 0.5 s per crossfade — a genuine seconds/milliseconds unit mismatch. Only defect; other conversions (load_playlist *1000, format_duration /1000, check_ad_ratio /1000, duration_ms/1000 in the same function) are correct distractors. 4 files. locality_hops=3 is defensible counting the cross-file import plus two calls (generate_daily_log->build_hourly_log->_accumulate_duration). Keys are plausible and none appear verbatim. No hints, no execution output.

blind_review.description: average_soil_moisture blends read_capacitance_probe (a volumetric water fraction, 0.0-1.0) with read_watermark_sensor (a percent of field capacity, 0-100) without converting them to a common scale. The percent value dominates and the resulting 'moisture' is then compared against WILTING_POINT/FIELD_CAPACITY, which are fractions, so the water stress calculation is meaningless.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault: average_soil_moisture blends read_capacitance_probe (VWC fraction 0.0-1.0) with read_watermark_sensor (percent 0-100) and averages them without conversion, then compares against WILTING_POINT/FIELD_CAPACITY on the 0-1 scale. Mixed units / different scale, no conversion. Keys apt and none appear verbatim (docstrings say 'Convert' but not 'without conversion'/'mixed units'/'different scale'). 5 files; 4 call hops main->report->estimate->stress->average; ~4 correct unit-conversion distractors (hectares, watermark curve, grams->kg, kg/bin). Exactly one defect.

blind_review.description: congestion_multiplier divides the raw vehicle count from a 300-second (5-minute) sampling window by RATED_CAPACITY_VPH, which is a per-hour rating. A 5-minute count is compared against an hourly capacity without scaling by 3600/window_seconds, so utilization is understated by ~12x and the surcharge essentially never triggers.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault: congestion_multiplier divides window.count() (vehicles observed in a 300s = 5-minute window) by RATED_CAPACITY_VPH (vehicles/hour) without converting time bases; utilization is understated by ~12x. Keys match, none verbatim, single units defect, no hints, no execution output.

blind_review.description: items_needing_pull uses bisect_left, which excludes items whose days_until_expiry exactly equals action_window_days. Since the docs say pull everything expiring 'within the given number of days,' an item expiring exactly at the window boundary should be included, so it should use bisect_right.

metadata_audit.notes: The boundary fault is real: items_needing_pull uses bisect_left(thresholds, action_window_days), which excludes items whose days_until_expiry exactly equals action_window_days, even though the docstring says items must be pulled 'within the given number of days' (inclusive of the boundary day). bisect_right would be correct. Keys plausibly describe this and none appear verbatim. summarize_pull's <=0/>0 split is correct, so single_defect holds; it is arguably a minor boundary distractor but not clearly enough to falsify distractor_count=0.

blind_review.description: The proration counts (end_date - start_date).days, but the docstring says both the start and end dates are billable service days, so it should be that difference plus one. As written it charges for one day too few (e.g. same-day start/end bills zero days).

The consecutive-days check flags a window of exactly max_consecutive (6) worked days as a violation, but working the maximum allowed number of days should be legal -- a violation only occurs when someone works max_consecutive+1 (7) days in a row. The window should span max_consecutive+1 days.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is in is_overworked_window: range(max_consecutive) builds a window of only max_consecutive (6) days, so working exactly 6 consecutive days is flagged even though max_consecutive=6 should permit it; a violation requires max_consecutive+1 (7) consecutive days, so the window is one day short. This matches all recorded keys, none of which appear verbatim. Hops: audit_roster -> check_consecutive_days -> is_overworked_window = 2. Single file. Distractors (build_worked_days inclusive while-loop, check_consecutive_days inclusive while and check_rest_periods zip pairing) plausibly total ~2. Employee-mixing in the two checks reads as single-employee-roster design (no employee grouping anywhere), not a second fault. No hints, no tests/output.

blind_review.description: The window length used to prove a sustained event is off by one: span = int(min_duration_s // interval_s) readings only span (span-1)*interval_s seconds of time, so it accepts stretches that are one interval short of min_duration_s. To cover at least min_duration_s with evenly spaced samples you need min_duration_s // interval_s + 1 readings.

In _locate_segment the binary search upper bound is set to len(cumulative) - 3, but the largest valid segment index is len(cumulative) - 2. This makes the last route leg unreachable, so any target distance falling in the final segment is interpolated on the wrong (earlier) segment; with only 3 waypoints the search collapses to always returning 0.

The overage fee is computed against plan.max_ride_minutes (the lost-bike threshold) instead of plan.free_minutes, which is the plan's covered/free minutes. As a result free_minutes is never used, and riders are only billed after exceeding the max-ride limit rather than after their free allotment.

metadata_audit.notes: The fee is computed against plan.max_ride_minutes (the lost-bike/abandonment cutoff) instead of plan.free_minutes, the plan's covered minutes per the docstring; free_minutes is never used. This is a single comparison/threshold fault. Keys are plausible and none appear verbatim (field names use underscores, e.g. free_minutes vs 'free minutes'). Covariates fit: fault in the entry function (0 hops), 1 file, ~6 other correct comparison sites as distractors. No hints and no execution output.

blind_review.description: In _interval_for_patient the pharmacy-consult check tests the patient's age against CONSULT_PHARMACY_THRESHOLD_CRCL (a creatinine-clearance limit of 20), when it should test crcl. As written, no adult's age is below 20 so the consult path never triggers, and patients with dangerously low CrCl get a standard interval instead of individualized dosing.

metadata_audit.notes: The single fault is in _interval_for_patient: `if age < CONSULT_PHARMACY_THRESHOLD_CRCL` compares age against a CrCl threshold (should be crcl). Keys match, none appear verbatim. locality_hops=1 (entry -> _interval_for_patient), files_spanned=1 correct. Other formulas (Cockcroft-Gault, IBW, adjusted body weight) are all standard/correct, so single_defect holds; distractor_count=0 is defensible.

blind_review.description: In _advance_row the vertical exhaustion check compares cursor_y + bmp.height against self.atlas_width, but it should compare against self.atlas_height. It tests the wrong dimension, so non-square atlases will detect exhaustion at the wrong point (or never/too early).

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is in _advance_row: `self.cursor_y + bmp.height > self.atlas_width` should compare against atlas_height (vertical axis) but uses atlas_width. Comparison/wrong-axis defect confirmed. Keys are plausible and none appear verbatim. locality_hops=2 (pack_glyphs -> place -> _advance_row), files=1, distractor=1 (the correct horizontal check in place). No unmarked hints, no execution display.

blind_review.description: The steer-axle reading is compared against the drive-axle limit (34000) and the drive-axle reading against the steer-axle limit (12000) -- the two limit constants are swapped, so a steer axle can be badly overweight without flagging while a legal drive axle gets flagged.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault is the cross-wired axle checks: steer_axle compared to FEDERAL_DRIVE_AXLE_LIMIT (34000) and drive_axle to FEDERAL_STEER_AXLE_LIMIT (12000). One comparison defect, keys not verbatim (code uses underscores/axle-group), no marks, no tests. All claims hold.

blind_review.description: In _split_by_affinity, 'favored' tracks are selected as those with skip_count ABOVE the average, so the queue preferentially picks the most-skipped (least-liked) tracks 75% of the time. Favored should be the tracks with skip_count below the average.

metadata_audit.notes: Fault: in _split_by_affinity, 'favored' collects tracks with skip_count > avg (high-skip = frequently skipped), then FAVORED_PICK_CHANCE=0.75 preferentially picks them; comparison is reversed (should be < avg to favor low-skip tracks). Keys fit and none appear verbatim; 1 hop from build_shuffle_queue to the fault; single defect.

blind_review.description: The float() parse catches ValueError alongside TypeError, so any container whose scale telemetry is present but unparseable (corrupt/garbled reading) gets silently dumped into pending_weigh and reported as 'awaiting scale' — even though it was weighed. Real bad-data errors are swallowed and mislabeled instead of being surfaced as a discrepancy or error; only None/empty should mean not-yet-weighed.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault: except (TypeError, ValueError) swallows both a missing reading (None->TypeError, empty->ValueError, legitimately pending) and a genuinely malformed non-empty telemetry string (ValueError), silently routing bad data into pending_weigh/zero instead of surfacing it. Keys describe this and none appear verbatim. locality_hops 0 (fault in entry function), 1 file, and several plausible-but-correct distractors (KeyError->ManifestError raise, sort key abs, over/under direction, surcharge calc) support distractor_count 3. No hints in names/comments/docstrings; no tests or output.

blind_review.description: GazeOffScreenError is documented as a normal, expected signal meaning the candidate looked away (a proctoring violation), but process_frame lumps it into the same except block as CorruptFrameError and treats it as a dropped frame: it logs a benign warning, records no violation, and returns early without counting the frame. A genuine look-away is silently discarded instead of being logged as a violation.

_rate_multiplier catches KeyError and silently returns the standard multiplier for any unrecognized rate_plan, so bad/mistyped plan data is swallowed and the guest is billed at full standard rate instead of the error being surfaced.

metadata_audit.notes: The single fault is the boundary check in _apply_rate_plan_and_validate: `nights <= 0` rejects legitimate zero-night/day-use/same-day reservations with a ValueError (should be `nights < 0`). Keys describe this scenario, none appear verbatim. locality_hops=2 (generate_billing_summary -> compute_charge -> _apply_rate_plan_and_validate). Distractors (KeyError fallback, date parsing, dict room-number overwrite, round, **r unpacking) support count=5. No cues or execution output.

blind_review.description: When every reading in a batch is skipped (accepted==0 and skipped>0), the function raises RuntimeError instead of returning the promised (total_kw, accepted, skipped) tuple. An all-bad batch is a valid, expected case that the docstring says should be handled by skipping and reporting counts, not by aborting.

metadata_audit.notes: The broad `except Exception` wraps `writer.writerow(...)`, so a genuine write/IO failure during logging is silently swallowed and miscounted as a skipped reading rather than propagating. Keys match this exception defect and none appear verbatim. Covariates plausible (in-function fault, 1 file, ~6 correct-but-pausable spots: clamping, negative check, id range, RuntimeError, header logic, isoformat parsing). No other faults; no hints; no execution output.

blind_review.description: renew_permit wraps the fee charge and record update in a bare `except Exception: return None`, which swallows the specific PermitError (insufficient balance) along with any other error. A distinct, valid business outcome that should be reported to the user is collapsed into a generic None, so describe_renewal tells the user to 'try again or contact support' instead of telling them their balance was too low.

The gain is computed as integrated_lufs - TARGET_LUFS, which is backwards. To move a mix onto the loudness target you need target minus measured (e.g. a -20 LUFS track needs +4 dB to reach -16), but this formula returns -4 dB, so quiet episodes get attenuated and loud ones get boosted.

In cancel_hold, after removing a hold the later holders should move UP to fill the gap, so their positions should decrease by one; instead the code does hold.position += 1, pushing them further back and leaving a gap.

metadata_audit.notes: Sole fault is in cancel_hold: holds behind the removed target have their position incremented (hold.position += 1) instead of decremented; keys describe this accurately and none appear verbatim; covariates fit.

blind_review.description: The deadline term is added, so tickets with more time left until their SLA deadline get a higher urgency score. Urgency should increase as the deadline approaches, so hours_until_deadline should lower the score (be subtracted), not raise it.

Yesterday's balance (goal - consumed) is subtracted from today's allowance, but the docs say finishing under goal should ADD room and over goal should tighten it. Since under-eating makes the balance positive, subtracting it wrongly reduces today's allowance; the term should be added instead.

The effective delivery rate INCREASES delivery with elevation, but pressure loss above the pump should REDUCE delivery. The formula uses (1 + PRESSURE_LOSS_PER_M * elevation_gain_m) where it should be (1 - ...), so higher zones are treated as watering faster instead of slower, under-watering them.

metadata_audit.notes: The sole fault is the flipped sign in _effective_delivery_rate: pressure loss should reduce delivery, so it should be (1 - PRESSURE_LOSS_PER_M * elevation_gain_m), but the code uses (1 + ...), increasing delivery with elevation. Daily-adjustment signs, deficit computation, and wilt-point comparison are all correct. Keys are plausible and none appear verbatim (the variable PRESSURE_LOSS_PER_M is uppercase/underscored, not the phrase 'pressure loss'). locality_hops=1 (entry compute_watering_duration -> _effective_delivery_rate), files_spanned=1, and distractor_count=2 (daily adjustment signs, deficit line) are reasonable.

blind_review.description: The liquid check adds up amounts in cups, tablespoons, and teaspoons directly without converting them to a common unit, then compares the mixed sum against a single threshold of 6.0. Since 1 cup = 16 tbsp = 48 tsp, these quantities are on wildly different scales and can't be summed as-is.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault: liquid_total sums amounts across 'cup', 'tbsp', 'tsp' without converting to a common unit before comparing to the 6.0 threshold, a genuine units defect. Keys are plausible and none appear verbatim. locality_hops=0 (fault in scale_recipe, the entry point), files_spanned=1 correct. distractor_count=1 is defensible (cube-root bake-time scaling is the salient plausible-but-correct pause point). No other faults; no marking; no execution display.

blind_review.description: In _total_engine_hours, idle_minutes (in minutes) is added directly to running_hours (in hours) without converting minutes to hours; it should be divided by 60 before being added.
MUTE_DURATION_MS is 5 minutes expressed in milliseconds (300000), but it's added directly to `now`, which is `time.time()` in seconds. So mutes last ~300000 seconds (~3.5 days) instead of 5 minutes.

metadata_audit.notes: MUTE_DURATION_MS (300000 ms) is added to a seconds-based timestamp (time.time()) in _mute_user, so mutes last 300000 seconds instead of 300. Fault is 2 hops from entry (moderate_message -> _maybe_mute -> _mute_user), single file, ~3 distractors (>SPAM_MESSAGE_LIMIT boundary, >= severity threshold, decay math, byte-length check). No verbatim key phrases, no hints, no output. All claims hold.

blind_review.description: The low-balance check compares post_disbursement_remaining, which is in cents, against LOW_BALANCE_ALERT_THRESHOLD_DOLLARS which is 500 dollars, without converting. It should compare against 500 * CENTS_PER_DOLLAR (50000 cents), so as written it only flags when the remaining balance drops below $5.00 instead of $500.

metadata_audit.notes: The fault is the low_balance test: post_disbursement_remaining (cents) is compared against LOW_BALANCE_ALERT_THRESHOLD_DOLLARS (500 dollars), a factor-of-100 unit mismatch; it should be multiplied by CENTS_PER_DOLLAR. Keys describe this, none appear verbatim. locality_hops 0 (fault in entry function), 1 file, ample distractors (fee rounding, net-vs-gross remaining, cooldown math). No unmarked hints; print does not expose the bug.

blind_review.description: The AGC gain is given as a percent (e.g. 20.0 for 20%), but _to_ground_velocity treats it as a raw fraction: gain_correction = 1.0 + agc_gain_percent yields 21.0 instead of 1.2, so it should divide by 100 first.

metadata_audit.notes: The one fault is in _to_ground_velocity: gain_correction = 1.0 + agc_gain_percent treats a percentage (20.0) as a raw fraction, missing the divide-by-100 conversion. Keys all fit and none appear verbatim. Fault is 1 call hop from the entry point, 1 file. Distractors (round in _seconds_to_samples, full_scale_counts/volts, window start/end clamping, sensitivity division) are plausible correct spots. main only prints sample count, not the miscalibrated values.
